hypothese.summary: Artisanal luxury house with a unique model (16 business lines, a near-monopoly in very high-end Birkin/Kelly leather goods, deep vertical integration, ~75% of production in France) showing the strongest resilience in the sector: uninterrupted growth even in 2025 in a broadly declining luxury market. H1 2026 confirms a sequential acceleration (Q2 +7% at constant exchange rates vs Q1) and a recurring operating margin close to historical highs (41%), but the market marked the stock down (-4,7% to -5,2% on the day of the release) against a backdrop of modest reported growth (+2% at current exchange rates, FX effect of -360M€) and caution on margins. Key point identified in the transcript: an exceptional surtax on the profits of large French companies weighs ~8pts on the 2025-2026 tax rate but is explicitly presented by management as a time-limited measure (the average of the 2025-2026 fiscal years only) - the source of a mechanical rebound in net income expected as early as 2027.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Hermes is the structurally hardest-to-imitate franchise in luxury: 16 metiers anchored on leather goods (44% of sales), 15-18 hours of hand-stitching per bag, deliberate scarcity over volume, ~75% production in France, 66.7% family control, and a net cash pile of 12.9bn EUR - the group has NEVER carried net debt and never printed a declining quarter through the 2023-2025 luxury downturn (unlike LVMH, Kering, Richemont). Sales nearly doubled 2021-2025 (8.98 -> 16.0bn EUR) with recurring operating margin up every year to 41.1%. S1 2026 extends the pattern: +6% cc (Q2 accelerating to +7%), margin 41% despite ~200M EUR of FX drag, net 2.2bn EUR - yet the stock fell ~5% on reported-growth optics (+2% at current FX, -4.5pts of FX). The one modeling-critical item: France's exceptional corporate surtax costs ~360M EUR in 2026 (270 already booked in S1, ETR 35.4%) and is explicitly limited to FY2025-2026 per the CFO - hence a MECHANICAL net-income rebound in 2027 (ETR back to 27.5%) independent of any operating improvement, fully carried by the bridge.

== THESIS READ ==
- Q2 accelerated to +7% cc with margin held at 41% against a 200M EUR FX hit - the scarcity model keeps pricing through everything; capacity stays deliberately constrained (one new leather workshop per year to 2030).
- The 2027 net rebound is fiscal, not operational: surtax (35% ETR) ends with FY26 - EPS steps from 42.6 to 51.5 EUR largely on tax normalization; do not read it as acceleration.
- China 'stabilized, not improving' (CEO) - aspirational buyers weak, wealthy clientele resilient; the CEO's own early-warning proxy (pork prices) tracked in the watch-list.
- Perfume is the one soft spot (-4%), acknowledged as underperforming outside own boutiques.
- Watch: France (+2%) vs rest-of-Europe (+9%) gap - resorption expected with Middle-East tourist flows; a persistent gap would flag domestic softness.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None structurally recurring. Note (not a valuePct item): the dividend policy is deliberately irregular, with frequent exceptional distributions (10 EUR in 2023 and 2024, 3 EUR in 2025) - headline yield is not representative of a linear policy.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: Hermes' published recurring operating income (clean by construction, no E5-e retreatment). FY26 bottom-up: S1 published 8.2bn + S2 ~8.24bn EUR (~+7% cc, conversion FX ~0 at current parities) -> ~16.4bn (+2.5% reported); margin 40.5% (hedging cost heavier in H2 per the CFO: ~210M EUR FY vs ~100M in S1). Bridge (c-ter): reconciles exactly - tax 35% in 2026 (surtax, front-loaded 75% in S1) then 27.5% from 2027; growing interest income on the cash pile (+225 -> +286M EUR; omniumND -13.5 -> -19.5bn). Shares flat 104.8M. Semiannual split kept (H1 26 ACTUAL 21.0 EUR published; H2 21.6 residual; NY 24.7/26.8 with a slight H2 bias, the 2026 surtax distortion NOT carried into 2027). Scorecard: no-guidance house - anchor 41.0 EUR (implicit consensus, imperfect, re-anchor Feb 2027), history not measurable, application suspended (documented). basis set to null with the justification moved to AN-BASIS-NOTE (revenue-only consensus comparison at S1). WATCH-LIST: (1) effective surtax expiry in 2027 (political risk of reconduction); (2) China pork-price proxy / consumption signal; (3) France vs Europe gap resorption; (4) capex pace (~1bn EUR FY, H2-loaded) and the 26th leather workshop; (5) Swiss watchmaking and tableware site details from the interim report. Next useful refresh: Q3 revenue (22 Oct).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 revenue (22 Oct): sequential acceleration test and France/Europe gap; new bags (Double Longue, Kelly Hobo) from September; first couture collection January 2027; 2027 fiscal normalization.

ancrages.moteur: Hermès NEVER communicates a quantified target (a consistent policy for years) - only an 'ambitious target of revenue growth at constant exchange rates' over the medium term, reconfirmed unchanged at H1 2026. Rebuilt bottom-up: actual H1 2026 (~8 180 M€) + H2 2026 estimated at ~8 240 M€ (continued constant-currency growth close to the pace of Q2 2026, ~7%, with an FX effect that should move closer to neutral in translation over the year according to the CFO at current parities) - FY2026 total ~16 400 M€.

Continued constant-currency growth, robust but gradually less spectacular than over the 2021-2024 period (historical 2016-2026 CAGR of 13%/yr claimed by management), consistent with the constraint management has taken on of favouring artisanal quality/exclusivity over volume maximisation (one new leather-goods workshop per year, ~300 jobs each, a deliberately measured pace): reported growth taken at +7%/yr over 2027-2028 then +6,5%/yr over 2029-2030.

Recurring operating margin taken at 40,5% in FY2026 (slightly below H1 at 41%, with the FX hedging effect becoming heavier in H2 according to the CFO), then gradual improvement towards 41,8% in 2030 - consistent with the group's demonstrated historical trajectory (39,3% in 2021 to 41,1% in 2025, near-continuous improvement despite FX headwinds), with no assumption of a positive or negative break.

KEY ANCHOR identified in the H1 2026 transcript: the exceptional contribution on the profits of large French companies (a 41,2% surtax on the average corporate income tax charge for 2025-2026, ~360 M€ of estimated cost in FY2026) is explicitly described by the CFO as limited to the 2025 and 2026 fiscal years ONLY. Normative corporate tax rate taken at 35% for 2026 (consistent with the actual H1 2026 rate of 35,4%) then BROUGHT BACK TO 27,5% from 2027 (return to the normative rate excluding the surtax) - the driver of a significant mechanical rebound in net income in 2027, independent of any underlying operating improvement. Point of caution: no legislative extension of the surtax beyond 2026 has been identified at this stage, but it remains a political risk to be monitored (the French government could extend it).

Net financial income and share of profit of associates kept at a modest and stable level (~180-230 M€ and ~46-56 M€ respectively over the horizon), consistent with actual H1 2026 (90 M€ of financial income, 23 M€ of share of associates, mainly Middle East excluding the Emirates) and with a very high net cash position but interest rates and FX hedging costs that weigh moderately.

Share count kept stable at ~104,8M across the whole horizon - dilution historically almost nil at Hermès (buybacks limited to the liquidity contract and to employee share plans, a family governance structure at 66,7% little inclined to dilution).

Continued build-up of net cash (Hermès has never resorted to net debt) at a pace of around 1,3-1,5 Md€/yr, consistent with the historical trajectory (7,07 Md€ at end-2021 to 12,8 Md€ at end-2025) and with very high adjusted free cash flow generation (2,2 Md€ in H1 2026 alone, +18%) after operating investments (~1 Md€/yr) and dividends (variable, often >2 Md€/yr): net cash position projected at ~13,5 Md€ at end-2026, then continued growth towards ~19,5 Md€ at end-2030.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantified quarterly guidance (Hermès's consistent policy). Qualitative signal from the CFO: no change of trend observed in the United States, Japan, Korea and Europe for the rest of the year; the question marks are on France (where an improvement was already observed in Q2 vs Q1) and on the Middle East, whose trajectory remains inherently unpredictable according to management.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: Qualitative directional target reconfirmed unchanged: ambitious revenue growth at constant exchange rates over the medium term. No precise quantification provided, in line with the group's consistent policy of historically refusing any numerical guidance. Operating investments expected at ~1 Md€ for the full year (the usual acceleration in H2). 2027 pricing: the budget process is still too early for any quantification, but management already indicates that it expects a price increase 'slightly lower' than the one applied in 2026.
pointsCles: Q2 accelerated to +7% at constant currency (H1 +6%, revenue EUR 8.2bn) led by Americas +15%, Japan +11% and Europe ex-France +9%; leather goods rose +10% and management explicitly warned against mechanically adding 6% volume plus price to model the division - growth is measured in artisan hours, with one new leather workshop per year through 2030 (~300 jobs each) and quality of available leather as the real bottleneck.

Margins held at elite levels despite FX: recurring operating margin 41.0% (EUR 3.4bn) absorbing a ~EUR 200m currency drag (-1pt), gross margin up 0.4pt to 71.1% on record sell-through and near-zero working capital build; adjusted free cash flow +18% to EUR 2.2bn and restated net cash EUR 12.9bn (50% of equity).

China 'stabilized but not improving' per CEO Axel Dumas, with demand tied to the property market and household savings rather than GDP; aspirational customers under pressure globally while wealthy clients stay resilient, and the Middle East war shaved ~1.5pt off group growth in both Q1 and Q2 as Gulf clients stopped travelling (also hitting Paris stores).

Net income group share flat at EUR 2.2bn, dented by the exceptional French corporate surtax (EUR 270m in H1, ~EUR 360m expected FY26, limited to fiscal 2025-26), setting up a mechanical net income rebound in 2027; H2 faces a heavier hedging headwind (~EUR 210m FY vs EUR 100m in H1), capex acceleration to EUR 1bn and targeted sales-force hiring, while 2027 price increases are expected slightly below 2026.

hypothese.guidanceLongTerme: Hermès communicates no quantified medium- or long-term target, neither on revenue nor on margin - a consistent and deliberate group policy for years, reiterated at every release ('ambitious target of revenue growth at constant exchange rates'). The only near-quantifiable element communicated: a pace of roughly one new leather-goods workshop opening per year through 2030 (~300 jobs each), deliberately constrained so as to preserve artisanal exclusivity rather than to accelerate volumes. A new production site post-2030 is mentioned, in a region not specified at this stage.
